clue.text: Cheese bun deli has made up

indicators.note: something made up is invented or put together anew, so these letters are reassembled in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A deli sandwich: someone has assembled a cheese roll at the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' rearranges the ten letters of BUN DELI HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-veined soft variety from Denmark, a familiar type of fromage.

clue.text: Outspoken, shocking court

parts.note: something shocking is dreadful, dire

explanation.surface: A judge or tribunal is criticised for being blunt in a scandalous way.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: someone outspoken speaks plainly and frankly, without hedging.

clue.text: Certainly not included in population of Earth

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words population of Earth, spanning the word breaks

explanation.surface: A denial that something is counted among the people living on the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' points to letters running across the end of 'population', all of 'of' and the start of 'Earth'.
explanation.definitionFit: A British colloquial exclamation of refusal, meaning roughly 'not a chance'.

clue.text: Narrow piece sailor uncovered in game

parts.note: a strip is a long thin piece of something
Jack (as in Jack tar) is a traditional name for a sailor
naked means bare, without covering

explanation.surface: A sailor stripped bare while playing something, a scene of naval horseplay.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a children's card game, also called Beggar My Neighbour, in which one player tries to win the whole pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a simple card game for two in which players turn cards over until one holds the entire deck.

clue.text: A peer may have one, high tea with Corbyn

indicators.note: high suggests intoxicated, out of one's normal state, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An aristocrat sits down to a high tea with Jeremy Corbyn, the former Labour leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' rearranges TEA and CORBYN together; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary title ranking below a barony, which some members of the House of Lords also hold.

clue.text: Superior meal, no seconds required

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter for seconds is dropped from the meal

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A fine dinner so satisfying that nobody asks for a second helping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' looks like extra helpings but is just S, removed by 'no'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as adjectives: higher in rank or position, as in the higher class or deck.

clue.text: Shower coat

definitions.meaning: to shower someone with things is to throw them repeatedly, bombard

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to bombard with missiles or rain heavily, and an animal's skin with its fur.

clue.text: Former pit worker holding a marker

indicators.note: holding means the first pieces keep the next piece inside them

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a miner works down a pit, a coal mine

explanation.surface: A retired coal miner who now carries a pen or token of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marker' suggests a pen, but here it is someone who marks papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who marks exam scripts and grades the candidates' answers.

clue.text: Paper in stand is European

parts.note: to stand someone a drink is to treat them

explanation.surface: A newspaper on a news stand turns out to come from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand' is the verb, as in standing a round, not a newsstand.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal written study of a subject, the scholarly sense of paper or essay.

clue.text: Juliet has long rambles with notable novelist

parts.note: Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: rambles suggests wandering aimlessly, so these letters stray into a new order

parts.note: worthy means notable, deserving attention

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's heroine goes on long country walks with a famous author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambles' rearranges HAS LONG into OHNGALS; 'with' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the English writer of The Forsyte Saga, a Nobel laureate in literature.

clue.text: Speak of hesitation by official in game

indicators.note: by means next to, so the hesitation sits after the official

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, officiates in a match
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A match official dithers while calling a decision during play.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to mention or allude to something, as in 'she referred to the report'.

clue.text: Rogue in favour of splitting money returned

indicators.note: splitting means the first piece goes into the middle of the second, dividing it

parts.note: a rebate is money paid back
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A scoundrel supports breaking up a refund scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: an unprincipled scoundrel, a person of bad character.

clue.text: Climbing aid in hamper by leg

indicators.note: by means next to, so the leg piece follows

parts.note: to cramp is to restrict or hamper
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A climber's kit is stowed in a basket beside a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' is a verb here, not a basket. In cricket the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiked metal frame strapped to a boot to grip ice, an aid for mountaineers.

clue.text: Grow profusely in enclosure — impressively large display

parts.note: a run is a fenced area for animals, as in chicken run
a riot of colour is a vivid, abundant display

explanation.surface: A garden plant flourishes inside a fenced space, making a spectacular show.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: plants left unchecked spread wildly and abundantly.

clue.text: Awfully frail, he hates some of those practising alternative medicine

definitions.text: some of those practising alternative medicine

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so these letters are reworked into another order

explanation.surface: A weak man dislikes certain alternative therapists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' looks like an intensifier but rearranges FRAIL HE HATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: people claiming to cure illness through prayer or belief rather than conventional treatment.

clue.text: Speak at length from keep on Scottish river

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the keep comes first

parts.note: a hold is the stronghold or keep of a castle
the Forth flows into the sea at Edinburgh

explanation.surface: Someone lectures from a castle tower overlooking a river in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to talk lengthily and pompously, holding an audience captive.

clue.text: Mean to imbibe half of raki and fish

indicators.note: imbibe means drink in, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: stingy means mean with money

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters of raki

explanation.surface: A miser plans to drink some Turkish spirit along with a fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Raki is an aniseed spirit from Turkey; its first half RA goes into STINGY.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a flat ray with a venomous barbed tail, a kind of sea creature.

clue.text: Time for a celebration by a third at sea?

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A sailor wonders whether a party is due after a third of the voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: An anniversary of one's birth, the usual occasion for a party and cake.

clue.text: Psychiatrist's ploy with pushbike rider

parts.note: a trick is a ploy or ruse
a cyclist rides a bicycle

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist's scheme involving a person on a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. The answer is jocular British slang, punning on the sound of 'psychiatrist'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a humorous British term for a shrink or mental health doctor.

clue.text: House housing a fierce woman

indicators.note: housing means containing, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: Virgo is one of the twelve astrological houses, signs of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A building that is home to an aggressive woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is the zodiac sense, not a building; 'housing' then puts A inside VIRGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a domineering, violent or bad-tempered woman, a harridan.

clue.text: Large building left in order

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: a caste is a social order or class

explanation.surface: A big edifice left neat and tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large fortified residence, the classic stately stronghold.

clue.text: Very foolish person, the head, facing trial

indicators.note: facing means set in front of, so the head comes first

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
a case is a trial in court

explanation.surface: A dim person, the boss of an organisation, is about to stand trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the head' suggests a leader but is NUT, slang for one's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a crazy or idiotic person.

clue.text: Run further

definitions.meaning: in cricket a run not scored off the bat, such as a wide or bye

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, runs from wides, byes and no-balls are credited separately from the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a cricket run not credited to the batsman, and additional or more.

clue.text: State papers collected by Ms Poste, say

indicators.note: collected by means taken inside, so the papers go into the name

parts.note: Flora Poste is the heroine of Stella Gibbons's comic novel Cold Comfort Farm
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Documents are picked up by a woman named Poste, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks Flora as one example of a Ms Poste. Flora Poste is the heroine of the English comic novel Cold Comfort Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the US state forming the south-eastern peninsula, home to Miami.

clue.text: Gundog inflamed compiler

parts.note: inflamed skin is red
a setter compiles crosswords

explanation.surface: A furious crossword maker's sporting dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Irish breed with a chestnut coat, used for pointing out game birds.

clue.text: Feature of bird stuffed by artist

indicators.note: stuffed by means filled with, so the artist goes inside the bird

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A taxidermist painter's prize item: a bird stuffed by an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a distinguishing characteristic or quality.

clue.text: Toy taken from Tokyo youngster

indicators.note: taken from signals a run of letters lifted out of the next words

explanation.surface: A plaything is confiscated from a Japanese child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' points to letters spanning the end of 'Tokyo' and the start of 'youngster'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a spool on a string that spins down and climbs back up.

clue.text: Tearful, Charles, upset about my rejected love

indicators.note: about means around, so the anagram goes round the other pieces
upset means knocked over, so the letters are disordered
rejected means sent back, so the word my is read backwards

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Charles is distraught after his sweetheart turned him down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles the name into LACHRSE, and 'about' wraps it round the reversed pronoun plus the tennis zero. 'rejected' is what turns the pronoun round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: given to weeping, mournful.
